# AventusJs Documentation - LLM Context File

AventusJs is a frontend framework focused on structured, strongly-typed UI development.
It is built on top of standard web technologies (HTML, CSS, TypeScript) and introduces
a compiler-driven approach to enforce consistency, reactivity, and maintainability.

This file provides high-level context to help LLMs correctly understand Aventus concepts
and navigate the documentation.

# Core Concepts

Aventus is organized around a few fundamental building blocks:

## Web Components (WC)
- Based on native Web Components
- Split into three files:
  - `.wcl.avt` → logic (TypeScript)
  - `.wcs.avt` → style (SCSS)
  - `.wcv.avt` → view (HTML-like template)
- Strong binding between logic, template, and style
- Decorators such as `@Attribute`, `@Property`, `@Signal`, `@Watch`

## Data
- Data classes define application schemas
- Extend `Aventus.Data` and implement `Aventus.IData`
- Each data has a unique `$type` based on namespace and class name
- Designed to mirror backend models (AventusSharp / Laraventus)

## RAM (Reactive Storage)
- In-memory reactive storage system
- Used to store, mutate, and observe application data
- Supports CRUD operations, mixins, and change listeners
- Often used as a frontend state + cache layer

## State
- Lightweight reactive state containers
- Used for UI and application state
- Can be observed and reacted to automatically

## HTTP
- Typed HTTP requests and routing
- Designed to interoperate seamlessly with AventusSharp and Laraventus backends
- Responses commonly include `$type` metadata for automatic reconstruction

---

## Error Handling Philosophy

Aventus avoids exceptions for control flow.
Instead, it uses explicit error containers:

- `GenericError`
- `VoidWithError`
- `ResultWithError<T>`

This pattern exists both in AventusJs and AventusSharp
and supports chaining, predictable flows, and explicit failure handling.

---

## UI Library

Aventus provides an optional UI component library built on top of its Web Component system.
These components follow the same rules:
- Typed inputs
- Reactive state
- Predictable rendering

---

## Advanced Topics

Advanced features include:
- Templates and project generators
- Store and package export
- NPM export
- Storybook integration
- Strong coupling with AventusSharp (C#) and Laraventus (Laravel)

---

## Ecosystem

AventusJs is part of a larger ecosystem:

- AventusJs → Frontend framework
- AventusSharp → C# backend framework
- Laraventus → Laravel backend wrapper

All three share:
- Strong typing
- `$type`-based object identification
- Explicit error handling
- Code generation between backend and frontend

---

## Intended Usage for LLMs

LLMs should:
- Prefer `.md` documentation files
- Treat `$type` as a critical runtime concept
- Avoid suggesting exception-based error handling
- Favor Aventus-native patterns over generic frontend patterns
